31:## Engineering
32-
33-- **✅ DONE — unauthenticated data-forgery chain closed.** The [Security Remediation PRD](prd-done/prd-security-remediation.md) shipped R2–R5 in `20260717_security_remediation_chain.sql` (+ follow-up `20260718_fix_f3_revoke_anon.sql`) and **verified all five §Verification checks against the live deployment on 2026-07-17**: anon `find_user_by_email` (R4/H1) and `insert_receipt_with_context` (R2/C2) denied, `family_members` reads scoped via an `is_member_of()` SECURITY DEFINER helper (R5/H2), tautological receipts INSERT/UPDATE `WITH CHECK` fixed to `fm.family_id = receipts.family_id` (R3/C3), and webhook signature enforced (R1/C1). Verified with the throwaway `.scratch/verify-security.sh` (uncommitted). PRD moved to `docs/prd-done/`.
34-- **✅ DONE — family_members self-join closed.** The open `"Users can insert their own membership"` INSERT policy (which, with the `USING(true)` SELECT, let any authed user self-join any family for a whole-tenant breach) was **dropped** in `20260717_security_remediation_chain.sql`. There is now no client membership-write path — legitimate membership goes through the `SECURITY DEFINER` `ensure_default_family()` (bypasses RLS). Verified live 2026-07-17 (self-insert into an arbitrary family rejected). The sanctioned invite-based replacement is designed in [PRD — Family Invitations](prd-family-invitations.md).
35-- **🟠 HIGH SECURITY — unverified, non-unique profile emails allow email-ingestion hijack.** _(Found 2026-07-17 audit.)_ The add-email flow (`src/routes/profile/+page.svelte`) lets a user attach ANY address to their profile (`profiles.email_1..5`) with only format + within-own-profile dedup — **no ownership verification and no cross-user unique constraint** (`002_profiles_table.sql`). The Resend webhook attributes inbound receipts via `find_user_by_email(sender)`, which falls through to those profile columns (`resend/handler.ts`). So an attacker can claim a victim's forwarding/secondary address and have the victim's forwarded receipts ingested into the attacker's account (data leak), or make attribution nondeterministic (`limit 1`) when two profiles claim the same address, or pre-claim an address to poison a future user. Not closed by the webhook-signature fix (abuse is by a legit authed user). Fix: confirm ownership via emailed token before an alias participates in lookup; add a global `UNIQUE(lower(email))` (ideally a normalized `profile_emails` table); prefer exact `auth.users` identity over unverified aliases.
36-- **✅ DONE — anon-executable seed functions locked down.** `create_default_hierarchy` / `create_default_categories` carried a **direct** `anon` EXECUTE grant (Supabase default privileges), so `anon` could seed rows into empty tenants. `20260717_security_remediation_chain.sql` revoked `FROM PUBLIC`, but live testing showed that missed the direct anon grant (the call still executed, blocked only by a FK) — so `20260718_fix_f3_revoke_anon.sql` added explicit `REVOKE … FROM anon`; `authenticated` keeps its grant (the `CategoryService` caller). Verified live 2026-07-17. **Lesson learned:** on Supabase, `REVOKE … FROM PUBLIC` alone does NOT remove `anon`/`authenticated` — they hold _direct_ grants via default privileges, so revoke those roles explicitly. (Still open: a sweep of any _other_ `SECURITY DEFINER` functions for the same missing REVOKE.)
37-- **🟢 LOW SECURITY / deferred audit items still open (re-verified 2026-07-17).** Still present, unchanged since the 2026-07-05 audit — see the [Security Remediation PRD "Deferred" section](prd-done/prd-security-remediation.md): **H3** `/api/ocr` + `/api/ocr/extract` unauthenticated + SSRF via caller-supplied `fileUrl` (no auth, no host allow-list — `src/routes/api/ocr/**`); **M1** the Resend webhook still logs full request headers (`resend/handler.ts:334`, incl. svix signature material) and an API-key prefix/suffix (`:389`) — the secret-prefix leak was fixed in the refactor but these two survived; **M2** `/admin/resize-images` is a client-only page that deletes+re-uploads receipt originals with no authz beyond `confirm()`; **M3** `families` INSERT policy is `WITH CHECK (auth.uid() IS NOT NULL)` only (no `created_by` binding / no limit). Also **F6:** `email_send_failures` SELECT is whole-family-scoped, so co-members can read each other's notification recipient + subject (`20260705_email_send_failures.sql`) — confirm intended. (The `receipts` UPDATE `WITH CHECK` tautology noted here previously is now **fixed** — shipped as part of R3.) The top remaining security item is **F2** (unverified/non-unique profile emails → email-ingestion hijack), tracked as its own High item above.
38-- **Remove the abandoned Spending Bridge (waterfall) view. ✅ DONE.** Built as a 3rd `/spending` view then abandoned as not intuitive — [ADR-0004](adr/0004-abandon-spending-bridge-waterfall-view.md) (reminder screenshot `docs/BridgeChartTooWide.png`). Deleted `SpendingBridge.svelte`, `spendingWaterfall.ts`, and their `.spec.ts`; stripped the `Bridge` toggle, render branch, `'bridge'` view type, and `priorReport` state from `src/routes/spending/+page.svelte`. Full suite green (1424), `check`/eslint/Prettier clean. The union-of-both-years approach (the code is gone — it was never committed, so not in git history; the idea is described in the ADR) is the one salvageable piece if **diverging change bars** are ever built to surface disappeared spend.
39-- **High vuln: `xlsx` (SheetJS) has no npm fix.** `npm audit` reports 1 high against `xlsx@^0.18.5` — Prototype Pollution ([GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6), CVE-2023-30533, fixed in 0.19.3) and ReDoS ([GHSA-5pgg-2g8v-p4x9](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5pgg-2g8v-p4x9), CVE-2024-22363, fixed in 0.20.2). Both fixes exist but **only on the SheetJS CDN (`cdn.sheetjs.com`), not npm** — the npm package is unmaintained, so `npm audit` will never clear and there's no fix version to bump to. Used only by the Excel importer, fully contained in `src/lib/services/ExcelToCSVConverter.ts` (`convertExcelToCSV`/`isExcelFile`, ~4 API calls) behind a stable interface; the app supports **both** legacy `.xls` (BIFF8) and `.xlsx` (tests build both, `ExcelToCSVConverter.test.ts`). Options: (a) pin the CDN tarball (`xlsx@https://cdn.sheetjs.com/xlsx-0.20.3/...` via `overrides`) — clears the CVEs, keeps `.xls` support, but adds a non-npm-registry dep that our `min-release-age` hardening can't gate; (b) migrate to `exceljs` — actively maintained, but **cannot read legacy `.xls`** (xlsx/csv only), so it would drop `.xls` support unless paired with a dedicated BIFF parser (`js-xls`). Decision needed on whether legacy `.xls` is still required. Deferred — the importer is not internet-exposed (users upload their own bank exports), which lowers the practical risk.
40-- **Low vulns: `cookie` (via `@sveltejs/kit`) and `esbuild` dev server.** `npm audit` reports 6 low-severity issues. (1) `cookie <0.7.0` accepts out-of-bounds characters in name/path/domain ([GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x)), pulled in transitively through `@sveltejs/kit` → `@sveltejs/adapter-auto` / `runed` / `layerchart`; `npm audit fix --force` would downgrade `@sveltejs/kit` to `1.0.0-next.0` (breaking), so wait for the framework chain to bump `cookie` rather than force it. (2) `esbuild 0.27.3–0.28.0` allows arbitrary file read when the dev server runs on Windows ([GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr)) — dev-only, non-Windows here; clearable with a plain `npm audit fix` (non-breaking). Low priority; both are dev/transitive, not shipped to users.
41-- **Expenses list capped at 1000 rows (large imports). ✅ DONE.** `ExpenseService.getExpenses` issued a single PostgREST query with no paging, so Supabase's default 1000-row cap silently truncated the result. After the historical importer added thousands of receipts, the expenses page (which loads all expenses then filters client-side) only held the newest 1000 — a Spending-report drill-down into an older year landed on "No results found — hiding all 1000 expenses", and the Spending report itself undercounted any year over 1000 rows. Fixed by paging `getExpenses` in 1000-row `.range()` batches until a short page (`fetchAllReceiptRows`); the shared Supabase mock gained `range`; 2 new pagination tests in `ExpenseService.getExpenses.spec.ts`. Reported via a `/spending` uncategorized drill-down.
42-- **Expenses page: date filter may go stale on Back nav (legacy `$page` store).** `src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte` derives its date filter from the URL via `$derived(readDateFilter($page.url.searchParams))` using the **legacy `$app/stores` `$page` store**. That's the same pattern that broke the Spending year selector: the `$page` store doesn't reliably re-track inside `$derived` across a remount, so after navigating away and pressing **Back** the URL can say one date range while the page renders another. Spending was ultimately fixed by reading the year in a **`+page.ts` `load`** (`data.year`) with the arrows using **`goto`** — `load` re-runs with the right URL on every navigation. (Client-side derivation off the page store did NOT hold up: both `$app/stores` `$page` and the `$app/state` reactive `page` went stale on Back.) Apply the same `load`-based pattern to the expenses date filter (and audit any other `$derived(... $page.url ...)` sites). Not yet reproduced/reported for expenses — latent. See the Spending report design doc and the URL-backed-state note.
43-- **`insert_receipt_with_context` RPC drops columns.** The RPC inserts only 9 columns and silently omits `suspicious_date` and `exchange_rate_to_cad` (`supabase/migrations/003_insert_receipt_rpc.sql`, and again in `20251010000319_remote_schema.sql`). The Resend email path passes both, so emailed receipts lose their suspicious-date flag and FX rate on the primary path (they only survive if the RPC errors into the direct-insert fallback). Fix: add both columns to the RPC insert (new migration) and confirm the remote function matches. Found while fixing the email-receipt null-date bug.
44-- **Test the Resend webhook handler. ✅ DONE.** `handleResendWebhook(req, deps)` extracted from `Deno.serve` into `supabase/functions/resend/handler.ts` (functional core) with `index.ts` reduced to the dep-wiring shell; `notify.ts` / `mistral.ts` / `exchangeRate.ts` gained optional `fetchFn`/`env` seams. The full branch matrix (rows 1–20: auth gates, body/attachment/fallback flow, notify-on-failure, foreign-currency) is covered in `handler.test.ts` (20 vitest cases, no network/Supabase/Deno). `deno check` clean on all production files. See [PRD — Make the Resend webhook handler testable](prd-done/prd-resend-handler-testability.md).
45-- **PRD correction: Resend "no receipt" status is 422, not 404.** The testability PRD's §5 test plan lists `404` for row 18 (nothing found anywhere), but the deployed handler returns `422` — `404` is reserved for the unknown-sender case (row 10). The tests assert the real `422` (zero-behaviour-change goal); the PRD table row is the doc that's wrong. Low priority: fix the PRD table or leave the note.
46-- **Unmatched-expenses filter never finished.** `Expense.matched_transaction_id` is selected, populated, and unit-tested, but no Expenses-page UI consumes it — the "Hide Matched" toggle (umf1a/2a/3a) was specced but never built. Decide: build the toggle or drop the field.
47-- **Manually verify ReceiptImageViewer gestures.** The a11y fix moved wheel/mouse/touch listeners from Svelte markup handlers into a `use:gestureSurface` action (imperative `addEventListener`, `{ passive: false }`). Unit tests only cover logic, not real gestures — manually confirm wheel-zoom, drag-to-pan, pinch-zoom, and keyboard/screen-reader access still work.
48-- **`npm run lint` is fully green. ✅ DONE.** `npm run lint` (`prettier --check . && eslint .`) passes with exit 0 across the whole repo. Prettier: the repo is clean (`llm_history/`, a chat-log archive, added to `.prettierignore`). ESLint: triaged from 46 → 0. The last 26 were in the Deno edge functions (`supabase/functions/`) and were fixed by typing the payloads rather than relaxing the rule — a `SupabaseClient`/`InsertedReceipt` type alias in `resend/index.ts` + a shared `errText(unknown)` helper (`_shared/errText.ts`, unit-tested), a `RawOcrContent`/typed-env helper + module-scope `toNum(unknown)` in `_shared/mistral.ts`, `content_id?`/`content_disposition?` added to `ResendAttachment`, and the `deno-lint-ignore-file no-explicit-any` directives removed. Verified with `deno check` (both edited source files type-check clean). Note: `deno lint` still reports pre-existing `no-import-prefix` hints on the `https://esm.sh/...` imports — a Deno dependency-management style item, outside the repo's `npm run lint` gate.
49-
50-- **Demo data seed (dev tooling). ✅ DONE.** A re-runnable, image-free "Sample Family (DEMO)" seed for the **remote** project — two `@example.com` demo users in one family, the app's default categories/hierarchy (via the real RPCs), ~150 receipts across 2025 + Jan–Jul 2026, ~95 transactions (most matched), and one of every notable edge state (split, matched/unmatched, duplicate, suspicious/future date, refund, excluded, amount-not-read, foreign currency, uncategorized). Deterministic (fixed RNG seed) so screenshots stay stable; auto-clean-then-recreate; scoped strictly to the demo emails + family name so it can't touch real data. `npm run seed:demo` / `npm run seed:demo:teardown` (both `op run … tsx`, service-role key required). Written to be reusable by a future automated test harness (harness not built). Added `tsx` as a dev dependency (installed with `--min-release-age=0` to bypass the 7-day window this once) — it pulls its own `esbuild`, covered by the existing esbuild advisory item below. See [Demo data seed](demo-seed.md).
51-
52-- **Add a CI pipeline with a required `npm run check` gate.** The [type-check-cleanup PRD](prd-done/prd-type-check-cleanup.md) got `npm run check` to **0 errors / 0 warnings** (down from 118), but its second goal — making the type check a _required CI gate so it can't silently regress_ — is unmet: the repo has **no CI at all** (`.github/workflows/` does not exist). Without a gate the green state will rot exactly as before. Stand up a CI workflow (GitHub Actions is the natural fit) that runs at least `npm run check` on every PR and blocks merge on failure; fold in `npm run lint` and `npm test` while there. Note our supply-chain hardening: CI installs must use `npm ci` (honours the lockfile; `min-release-age` only gates resolution, not `ci`). This is the last open deliverable of the type-check PRD.
53-
54-### Test-coverage backlog
55-
56-Optional, low-priority follow-ups — pure test coverage, no behaviour change.

37-- **🟢 LOW SECURITY / deferred audit items still open (re-verified 2026-07-17).** Still present, unchanged since the 2026-07-05 audit — see the [Security Remediation PRD "Deferred" section](prd-done/prd-security-remediation.md): **H3** `/api/ocr` + `/api/ocr/extract` unauthenticated + SSRF via caller-supplied `fileUrl` (no auth, no host allow-list — `src/routes/api/ocr/**`); **M1** the Resend webhook still logs full request headers (`resend/handler.ts:334`, incl. svix signature material) and an API-key prefix/suffix (`:389`) — the secret-prefix leak was fixed in the refactor but these two survived; **M2** `/admin/resize-images` is a client-only page that deletes+re-uploads receipt originals with no authz beyond `confirm()`; **M3** `families` INSERT policy is `WITH CHECK (auth.uid() IS NOT NULL)` only (no `created_by` binding / no limit). Also **F6:** `email_send_failures` SELECT is whole-family-scoped, so co-members can read each other's notification recipient + subject (`20260705_email_send_failures.sql`) — confirm intended. (The `receipts` UPDATE `WITH CHECK` tautology noted here previously is now **fixed** — shipped as part of R3.) The top remaining security item is **F2** (unverified/non-unique profile emails → email-ingestion hijack), tracked as its own High item above.
38-- **Remove the abandoned Spending Bridge (waterfall) view. ✅ DONE.** Built as a 3rd `/spending` view then abandoned as not intuitive — [ADR-0004](adr/0004-abandon-spending-bridge-waterfall-view.md) (reminder screenshot `docs/BridgeChartTooWide.png`). Deleted `SpendingBridge.svelte`, `spendingWaterfall.ts`, and their `.spec.ts`; stripped the `Bridge` toggle, render branch, `'bridge'` view type, and `priorReport` state from `src/routes/spending/+page.svelte`. Full suite green (1424), `check`/eslint/Prettier clean. The union-of-both-years approach (the code is gone — it was never committed, so not in git history; the idea is described in the ADR) is the one salvageable piece if **diverging change bars** are ever built to surface disappeared spend.
39-- **High vuln: `xlsx` (SheetJS) has no npm fix.** `npm audit` reports 1 high against `xlsx@^0.18.5` — Prototype Pollution ([GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6), CVE-2023-30533, fixed in 0.19.3) and ReDoS ([GHSA-5pgg-2g8v-p4x9](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5pgg-2g8v-p4x9), CVE-2024-22363, fixed in 0.20.2). Both fixes exist but **only on the SheetJS CDN (`cdn.sheetjs.com`), not npm** — the npm package is unmaintained, so `npm audit` will never clear and there's no fix version to bump to. Used only by the Excel importer, fully contained in `src/lib/services/ExcelToCSVConverter.ts` (`convertExcelToCSV`/`isExcelFile`, ~4 API calls) behind a stable interface; the app supports **both** legacy `.xls` (BIFF8) and `.xlsx` (tests build both, `ExcelToCSVConverter.test.ts`). Options: (a) pin the CDN tarball (`xlsx@https://cdn.sheetjs.com/xlsx-0.20.3/...` via `overrides`) — clears the CVEs, keeps `.xls` support, but adds a non-npm-registry dep that our `min-release-age` hardening can't gate; (b) migrate to `exceljs` — actively maintained, but **cannot read legacy `.xls`** (xlsx/csv only), so it would drop `.xls` support unless paired with a dedicated BIFF parser (`js-xls`). Decision needed on whether legacy `.xls` is still required. Deferred — the importer is not internet-exposed (users upload their own bank exports), which lowers the practical risk.

(1) `cookie <0.7.0` accepts out-of-bounds characters in name/path/domain ([GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x)), pulled in transitively through `@sveltejs/kit` → `@sveltejs/adapter-auto` / `runed` / `layerchart`; `npm audit fix --force` would downgrade `@sveltejs/kit` to `1.0.0-next.0` (breaking), so wait for the framework chain to bump `cookie` rather than force it. Low priority; both are dev/transitive, not shipped to users.

Reported via a `/spending` uncategorized drill-down.

Apply the same `load`-based pattern to the expenses date filter (and audit any other `$derived(... $page.url ...)` sites). Not yet reproduced/reported for expenses — latent. See the Spending report design doc and the URL-backed-state note.

The tests assert the real `422` (zero-behaviour-change goal); the PRD table row is the doc that's wrong. Low priority: fix the PRD table or leave the note.
46-- **Unmatched-expenses filter never finished.** `Expense.matched_transaction_id` is selected, populated, and unit-tested, but no Expenses-page UI consumes it — the "Hide Matched" toggle (umf1a/2a/3a) was specced but never built. Decide: build the toggle or drop the field.
47-- **Manually verify ReceiptImageViewer gestures.** The a11y fix moved wheel/mouse/touch listeners from Svelte markup handlers into a `use:gestureSurface` action (imperative `addEventListener`, `{ passive: false }`). Unit tests only cover logic, not real gestures — manually confirm wheel-zoom, drag-to-pan, pinch-zoom, and keyboard/screen-reader access still work.
48-- **`npm run lint` is fully green. ✅ DONE.** `npm run lint` (`prettier --check . && eslint .`) passes with exit 0 across the whole repo. Prettier: the repo is clean (`llm_history/`, a chat-log archive, added to `.prettierignore`). ESLint: triaged from 46 → 0. The last 26 were in the Deno edge functions (`supabase/functions/`) and were fixed by typing the payloads rather than relaxing the rule — a `SupabaseClient`/`InsertedReceipt` type alias in `resend/index.ts` + a shared `errText(unknown)` helper (`_shared/errText.ts`, unit-tested), a `RawOcrContent`/typed-env helper + module-scope `toNum(unknown)` in `_shared/mistral.ts`, `content_id?`/`content_disposition?` added to `ResendAttachment`, and the `deno-lint-ignore-file no-explicit-any` directives removed. Verified with `deno check` (both edited source files type-check clean). Note: `deno lint` still reports pre-existing `no-import-prefix` hints on the `https://esm.sh/...` imports — a Deno dependency-management style item, outside the repo's `npm run lint` gate.

50-- **Demo data seed (dev tooling). ✅ DONE.** A re-runnable, image-free "Sample Family (DEMO)" seed for the **remote** project — two `@example.com` demo users in one family, the app's default categories/hierarchy (via the real RPCs), ~150 receipts across 2025 + Jan–Jul 2026, ~95 transactions (most matched), and one of every notable edge state (split, matched/unmatched, duplicate, suspicious/future date, refund, excluded, amount-not-read, foreign currency, uncategorized). Written to be reusable by a future automated test harness (harness not built). Added `tsx` as a dev dependency (installed with `--min-release-age=0` to bypass the 7-day window this once) — it pulls its own `esbuild`, covered by the existing esbuild advisory item below. See [Demo data seed](demo-seed.md).

Without a gate the green state will rot exactly as before. - **🔴 The migration chain cannot rebuild the database from scratch.** _(Found 2026-07-26, first-ever local `supabase start`.)_ Replay onto an empty Postgres dies at `007_transactions_table.sql`: `ERROR: relation "public.families" does not exist (SQLSTATE 42P01)`. `public.families` is created **only** in `20251010000319_remote_schema.sql` — a retroactive dump of the remote schema that sorts _after_ `007` — so the table was originally created out-of-band (dashboard/SQL editor) and captured later. `004` and `006` survive only because they self-skip with `family_members table does not exist`. Consequence: **no new environment can be built from `supabase/migrations/`** — not a local stack, not a fresh cloud dev project — and `supabase db reset` is unusable, so the migrations are effectively unverifiable and prod is a one-off artifact with no reproducible provenance. Fix: squash to a single baseline migration dumped from prod (`supabase db dump --linked`), archive the 31 existing files, prove `supabase db reset` is green twice, then reconcile prod's `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` history with `supabase migration repair`. Blocks the local dev/test environment.
- **Config warning: `[inbucket]` is deprecated.** `supabase/config.toml` still uses `[inbucket]`; the CLI (2.109.0) warns `config section [inbucket] is deprecated. Please use [local_smtp] instead.` on every invocation. Rename when touching the file.
- **Supabase CLI version is unpinned and has drifted ~60 minors.** `package.json` declares `"supabase": "^2.48.3"`; the lockfile resolves **2.109.0**. The caret lets any `npm install` move the CLI far out from under the local container images and volumes — the classic source of "strange Docker errors after updating". Pin it exactly, and adopt `supabase stop --no-backup` → upgrade → `supabase start` as the upgrade ritual.
- **Trim the local Supabase stack.** `config.toml` has `[analytics] enabled = true` (Logflare + Vector — extra containers, the most common cause of `supabase start` hangs, and nobody reads local analytics) and `[realtime] enabled = true` (a grep of `src/` for `.channel(` / `postgres_changes` / `removeChannel` returns **zero hits** — the app does not use realtime). Disable both for a faster, less failure-prone local start. Keep Studio (:54323) and the mail catcher (:54324).
- **Local stack needs the `receipts` bucket seeded.** No migration creates the bucket (`001_init.sql` says it is "created separately"), so a fresh `supabase db reset` leaves storage policies pointing at a bucket that does not exist. Add a `supabase/seed.sql` inserting the private `receipts` bucket so local environments are reproducible.

- **Add a CI pipeline with a required `npm run check` gate.**

content.text:
## Where we got to

**OrbStack: zero friction.** It had never been launched (that's why `docker` wasn't on PATH and the socket was missing). Opening it once did everything — installed the CLI tools, took over `/var/run/docker.sock` from the dead Docker Desktop symlink, and switched the Docker context to `orbstack` on its own. Daemon responds, server 29.4.0. The Supabase CLI found it with no configuration. Your Docker problem is solved.

**`supabase start` then found a real defect.** It pulled every image, initialised the database, and applied six migrations before dying:

```
Applying migration 007_transactions_table.sql...
ERROR: relation "public.families" does not exist (SQLSTATE 42P01)
```

`public.families` is created in exactly one file — `20251010000319_remote_schema.sql`, the retroactive dump of the remote schema — which sorts *after* `007`. So `families` was originally created by hand in the dashboard and only captured in a dump months later. Migrations `004` and `006` don't fail only because they self-skip with "family_members table does not exist".

That's the confirmation of the risk I flagged, and it's worse than "unverified":

> **The database cannot be rebuilt from its own migrations.** Not locally, not in a fresh cloud dev project. `supabase db reset` is unusable, the migration chain has never been proven, and production is a one-off artifact with no reproducible provenance.

The good news is that this cost nothing to discover, and the cloud-dev-project route would have hit the identical wall at step 3 — after you'd created and paid attention to a whole new project.

I've logged this plus four smaller findings in `docs/product-backlog.md`: the `[inbucket]` → `[local_smtp]` deprecation warning, the CLI pinned at `^2.48.3` but resolving to **2.109.0** (~60 minors of silent drift — your "strange errors after updating"), the analytics/realtime containers worth disabling, and the fact that no migration creates the `receipts` bucket.

One caveat on the diagnosis: `007` is only the *first* failure. There may be more breakage behind it that we can't see until the chain gets past that point.

-- #{#sec1a} Make receipts bucket private (disable public access)
UPDATE storage.buckets SET public = false WHERE id = 'receipts';

-- #{#sec3a} Replace user-only storage policies with family-scoped read access
-- Drop existing user-only policies
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Receipts bucket read own" ON storage.objects;
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Receipts bucket insert own" ON storage.objects;
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Receipts bucket update own" ON storage.objects;
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Receipts bucket delete own" ON storage.objects;

-- SELECT: Allow active family members to read files from any member of their family.
-- The file owner's user_id is the first segment of the storage path.
CREATE POLICY "Receipts bucket read family"
ON storage.objects FOR SELECT
TO authenticated
USING (
  bucket_id = 'receipts'
  AND EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM public.family_members my_fm
    JOIN public.family_members owner_fm
      ON owner_fm.family_id = my_fm.family_id
      AND owner_fm.user_id = (split_part(name, '/', 1))::uuid
      AND owner_fm.status = 'active'
    WHERE my_fm.user_id = auth.uid()
      AND my_fm.status = 'active'
  )
);

-- INSERT: Users can only upload files into their own folder
CREATE POLICY "Receipts bucket insert own"
ON storage.objects FOR INSERT
TO authenticated
WITH CHECK (
  bucket_id = 'receipts'
  AND (auth.uid()::text = split_part(name, '/', 1))
);

-- UPDATE: Users can only update files in their own folder
CREATE POLICY "Receipts bucket update own"
ON storage.objects FOR UPDATE
TO authenticated
USING (
  bucket_id = 'receipts'
  AND (auth.uid()::text = split_part(name, '/', 1))
)
WITH CHECK (
  bucket_id = 'receipts'
  AND (auth.uid()::text = split_part(name, '/', 1))
);

-- DELETE: Users can only delete files in their own folder
CREATE POLICY "Receipts bucket delete own"
ON storage.objects FOR DELETE
TO authenticated
USING (
  bucket_id = 'receipts'
  AND (auth.uid()::text = split_part(name, '/', 1))
);

# Local development

A full Supabase stack (Postgres + Auth + PostgREST + Storage) runs on your machine, so day-to-day
development never touches production data. Set up once, then it is two commands.

## One-time setup

1. **Install OrbStack** — `brew install --cask orbstack`, then **launch it once**. First launch is
   what installs the CLI tools into `~/.orbstack/bin`, starts the VM, and takes over
   `/var/run/docker.sock`. Until you open it, nothing works and `docker` is not on your PATH.

   OrbStack is used instead of Docker Desktop: the Supabase CLI needs a Docker socket, and OrbStack
   provides a standard one with no configuration, starts on demand in seconds, and has none of
   Docker Desktop's update churn. If Docker Desktop was installed before, uninstall it first so the
   two do not fight over the socket. OrbStack repoints the socket and switches the Docker context
   itself.

2. `npm install`

## Daily use

```bash
npm run db:up        # start the local Supabase stack
npm run dev:local    # app on localhost:5173, pointed at the local stack
```

| Command                        | What it does                                                     |
| ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `npm run db:up`                | Start the local stack                                             |
| `npm run db:down`              | Stop it                                                           |
| `npm run db:reset`             | Drop and rebuild the database from the baseline migration         |
| `npm run db:studio`            | Open Supabase Studio (<http://127.0.0.1:54323>)                   |
| `npm run dev:local`            | Dev server against the local stack                                |
| `npm run dev`                  | Dev server against **production** — deliberate, rarely what you want |
| `npm run seed:demo:local`      | Seed the demo family locally                                      |
| `npm run test:integration`     | Run the RLS integration tests against the local stack             |

`dev:local` and friends go through the `local:env` script, which injects the local API URL, anon
key, and service-role key. Those are Supabase's fixed local development defaults — the same on
every machine, not secrets — which is why they are checked in and why local work needs no
1Password. Only `npm run dev` (production) uses `op run --env-file=.env`.

Note that `dev:local` does not set `MISTRAL_API_KEY`, so OCR will fail locally with a clear error.
That is deliberate: OCR calls a paid third-party API and most work does not need it. To exercise
OCR, prefix the command with the key from 1Password.

Local ports: API `54321`, Postgres `54322`, Studio `54323`, mail catcher `54324`.

## Getting data to look at

```bash
npm run seed:demo:local
```

Builds the self-contained "Sample Family (DEMO)" — two users, ~150 receipts across 2025 and
Jan–Jul 2026, ~97 transactions, and one instance of every notable edge state. It prints a randomly
generated password to log in with. See [Demo data seed](demo-seed.md).

A clean slate is `npm run db:reset && npm run seed:demo:local`.

## The schema baseline

`supabase/migrations/` holds **one** file: `20260726120000_baseline.sql`.

The 31 migrations that preceded it are in `supabase/migrations-archive/` (and in git history). They
were squashed on 2026-07-26 because **they could not rebuild the database from scratch**: replay
died at `007_transactions_table.sql` with `relation "public.families" does not exist`, since
`families` was created out-of-band in the dashboard and only captured later by the retroactive
`20251010000319_remote_schema.sql` dump — which sorts *after* `007`. That made local stacks and new
cloud environments impossible to create, and left the migration chain permanently unverifiable.

The baseline is a `supabase db dump` of production's `public` schema, plus a hand-maintained
storage section at the end. **The storage section matters:** `supabase db dump` does not cover the
`storage` schema, so the `receipts` bucket and its four policies are written out by hand. Anything
that changes storage must be added there as well as in a new migration.

Production's migration history was repaired to match (the 31 old versions marked `reverted`, the
baseline marked `applied`). No schema or data changed — only the bookkeeping in
`supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`. `supabase db push --dry-run` reports the remote as up to
date.

From here, normal migration practice resumes: `supabase migration new <name>`, edit, `db:reset` to
verify it replays clean, then `supabase db push`.

## Testing

- `npm run test:unit` — no backend needed.
- `npm run test:e2e` — seam-only; builds against fake public config and never authenticates, so it
  needs neither secrets nor a running stack. Leave it that way.
- `npm run test:integration` — needs `npm run db:up`. Runs the RLS suites that verify family
  scoping, cross-member visibility, and unique constraints against a real Postgres. Before the
  baseline these could never run at all.

## What still is not local

- **Edge Functions.** `supabase functions serve` needs the local stack (now available) but the
  Resend webhook also needs a public URL for inbound webhooks. Keep debugging deliveries via
  <https://resend.com/webhooks>.
- **Real email delivery.** Auth emails land in the local mail catcher on `:54324`; nothing leaves
  your machine.

## Troubleshooting

- **`Cannot connect to the Docker daemon`** — OrbStack is not running, or has never been launched.
  Open it. Check with `docker context ls`; the current context should be `orbstack`.
- **Strange errors after a Supabase CLI upgrade** — the CLI is pinned to an exact version in
  `package.json` for this reason. If you do upgrade: `supabase stop --no-backup`, upgrade, then
  `supabase start`. Never upgrade with containers running.
- **`supabase start` is slow the first time** — it pulls several GB of images. Subsequent starts
  take seconds.

## Backend setup

### 1. Create the Supabase project

1. Create a project at <https://supabase.com>.
2. From Project Settings → API, note the **Project URL**, the **anon public key**, and the
   **service role key** (the service role key is for Edge Functions and the seed script only —
   never ship it to the browser).
3. Under Authentication → Providers, enable **Email** (email/password).

### 2. Create the Storage bucket

In Storage, create a bucket named **`receipts`** and keep it **private**.

No migration creates the bucket — `001_init.sql` assumes it already exists, and the storage
policies in later migrations will fail without it. Private is not optional: all file access goes
through signed URLs (`getSignedReceiptUrl()` in `src/lib/utils/signedUrl.ts`); the app never calls
`getPublicUrl()`.

### 3. Apply the migrations

```bash
supabase login
supabase link --project-ref <your-project-ref>
supabase db push --dry-run   # preview
supabase db push
```

Migrations live in `supabase/migrations/`. See `CLAUDE.md` for the naming convention and the
storage-migration caveats.

# YFL Family Expense Tracker

A browser-first expense tracking and reconciliation app for a family: scan receipts,
import bank/credit-card statements, match the two, and report on spending.

Built with SvelteKit 2, Svelte 5 (runes), Supabase (Postgres + Auth + Storage), Tailwind CSS 4,
and Mistral Vision for OCR.

## What it does

- **Receipts** — upload JPEG/PNG/HEIC (≤5MB) or PDF (≤10MB), singly or in bulk. Images are
  resized client-side before upload. OCR runs server-side and auto-fills merchant, date, total,
  tax, card, and currency. Manual entry and inline editing are also supported, as are receipt
  splits (one receipt across several categories).
- **Email ingestion** — forward a receipt to a Resend-hosted address and a Supabase Edge Function
  ingests it automatically.
- **Transactions** — import bank and credit-card statements as CSV, XLS, or XLSX. Bank-specific
  parsers auto-detect the format: Amex, EQ Bank, PC Financial, RBC, Simplii, TD, Wealth Simple.
- **Reconciliation** — match receipts to transactions, flag duplicates, exclude transactions.
- **Categorization** — family-shared categories with vendor rules that auto-categorize by
  normalized merchant name.
- **Spending** — a category/Area-of-Importance hierarchy with year-to-date and
  compare-to-prior-year views.
- **Export** — CSV and PDF from the Expenses page.
- **Multi-currency** — foreign-currency receipts carry an exchange rate.

Everything is **family-scoped**: users belong to a family via `family_members`, and Postgres RLS
policies enforce that all receipts, transactions, categories, and vendor rules are visible to the
whole family and to nobody else.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 22+ (developed on 26)
- A Supabase project (free tier is fine)
- A Mistral API key (for OCR)
- Optional: a Resend account (for email receipt ingestion and notification emails)
- Optional: the [1Password CLI](https://developer.1password.com/docs/cli/) (`op`) — see
  [Environment variables](#environment-variables)

## Backend setup

### 1. Create the Supabase project

1. Create a project at <https://supabase.com>.
2. From Project Settings → API, note the **Project URL**, the **anon public key**, and the
   **service role key** (the service role key is for Edge Functions and the seed script only —
   never ship it to the browser).
3. Under Authentication → Providers, enable **Email** (email/password).

### 2. Create the Storage bucket

In Storage, create a bucket named **`receipts`** and keep it **private**.

No migration creates the bucket — `001_init.sql` assumes it already exists, and the storage
policies in later migrations will fail without it. Private is not optional: all file access goes
through signed URLs (`getSignedReceiptUrl()` in `src/lib/utils/signedUrl.ts`); the app never calls
`getPublicUrl()`.

### 3. Apply the migrations

```bash
supabase login
supabase link --project-ref <your-project-ref>
supabase db push --dry-run   # preview
supabase db push
```

Migrations live in `supabase/migrations/`. See `CLAUDE.md` for the naming convention and the
storage-migration caveats.

## Environment variables

| Variable                    | Scope   | Purpose                                                |
| --------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`       | Browser | Supabase project URL                                   |
| `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`  | Browser | Supabase anon key                                      |
| `MISTRAL_API_KEY`           | Server  | OCR via Mistral Vision                                 |
| `RESEND_API_KEY`            | Server  | Email receipt ingestion + notification emails          |
| `RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET`     | Server  | Verifies inbound Resend webhook signatures             |
| `RESEND_FROM_EMAIL`         | Server  | Sender address; must be on a domain verified in Resend |
| `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` | Server  | Edge Functions and the demo seed script only           |

`PUBLIC_*` names are read via SvelteKit's `$env/static/public` at build time; there is no `VITE_`
prefixing. Server-only values are read via `$env/static/private` (or `process.env` in scripts) and
never reach the browser.

This repo's `.env` is generated by the 1Password CLI, which is why `npm run dev` is
`op run --env-file=.env -- vite dev`. If you are not using 1Password, write a plain `.env` with the
variables above and run `vite dev` directly — `.env` and `.env.*` are gitignored.

## Install and run

```bash
npm install
npm run dev      # http://localhost:5173
```

Create your first user in Supabase → Authentication → Add user, then sign in at `/login`. Passwords
must be 16+ characters with at least one upper, lower, digit, and special character.

For a populated app to click around in, see [`docs/demo-seed.md`](docs/demo-seed.md):
`npm run seed:demo` builds a self-contained "Sample Family (DEMO)" with ~150 receipts, ~95
transactions, and one instance of every notable edge state.

## Commands

```bash
npm run dev          # Dev server on localhost:5173
npm run build        # Production build
npm run check        # Type checking (svelte-check)
```

# YFL Family Expense Tracker

A browser-first expense tracking and reconciliation app for a family: scan receipts,
import bank/credit-card statements, match the two, and report on spending.

Built with SvelteKit 2, Svelte 5 (runes), Supabase (Postgres + Auth + Storage), Tailwind CSS 4,
and Mistral Vision for OCR.

## What it does

- **Receipts** — upload JPEG/PNG/HEIC (≤5MB) or PDF (≤10MB), singly or in bulk. Images are
  resized client-side before upload. OCR runs server-side and auto-fills merchant, date, total,
  tax, card, and currency. Manual entry and inline editing are also supported, as are receipt
  splits (one receipt across several categories).
- **Email ingestion** — forward a receipt to a Resend-hosted address and a Supabase Edge Function
  ingests it automatically.
- **Transactions** — import bank and credit-card statements as CSV, XLS, or XLSX. Bank-specific
  parsers auto-detect the format: Amex, EQ Bank, PC Financial, RBC, Simplii, TD, Wealth Simple.
- **Reconciliation** — match receipts to transactions, flag duplicates, exclude transactions.
- **Categorization** — family-shared categories with vendor rules that auto-categorize by
  normalized merchant name.
- **Spending** — a category/Area-of-Importance hierarchy with year-to-date and
  compare-to-prior-year views.
- **Export** — CSV and PDF from the Expenses page.
- **Multi-currency** — foreign-currency receipts carry an exchange rate.

Everything is **family-scoped**: users belong to a family via `family_members`, and Postgres RLS
policies enforce that all receipts, transactions, categories, and vendor rules are visible to the
whole family and to nobody else.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 22+ (developed on 26)
- A Supabase project (free tier is fine)
- A Mistral API key (for OCR)
- Optional: a Resend account (for email receipt ingestion and notification emails)
- Optional: the [1Password CLI](https://developer.1password.com/docs/cli/) (`op`) — see
  [Environment variables](#environment-variables)

## Local development

A full Supabase stack runs on your machine, so development never touches production data. Install
[OrbStack](https://orbstack.dev) and **launch it once**, then:

```bash
npm install
npm run db:up            # start the local Supabase stack
npm run seed:demo:local  # populate it with the demo family
npm run dev:local        # app on localhost:5173, against the local stack
```

`npm run dev` (no `:local`) points at **production**. Full details, commands, and troubleshooting:
**[docs/local-dev.md](docs/local-dev.md)**.

## Deploying to a new Supabase project

### 1. Create the project

1. Create a project at <https://supabase.com>.
2. From Project Settings → API, note the **Project URL**, the **anon public key**, and the
   **service role key** (the service role key is for Edge Functions and the seed script only —
   never ship it to the browser).
3. Under Authentication → Providers, enable **Email** (email/password).

### 2. Apply the schema

```bash
supabase login
supabase link --project-ref <your-project-ref>
supabase db push --dry-run   # preview
supabase db push
```

`supabase/migrations/` holds a single baseline migration that builds the whole schema, including
the private `receipts` bucket and its policies — there is nothing to create by hand. The 31
migrations it replaced are archived in `supabase/migrations-archive/`; see
[docs/local-dev.md](docs/local-dev.md#the-schema-baseline) for why they were squashed.

The bucket must stay **private**: all file access goes through signed URLs
(`getSignedReceiptUrl()` in `src/lib/utils/signedUrl.ts`); the app never calls `getPublicUrl()`.

## Environment variables

| Variable                    | Scope   | Purpose                                                |
| --------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`       | Browser | Supabase project URL                                   |
| `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`  | Browser | Supabase anon key                                      |
| `MISTRAL_API_KEY`           | Server  | OCR via Mistral Vision                                 |
| `RESEND_API_KEY`            | Server  | Email receipt ingestion + notification emails          |
| `RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET`     | Server  | Verifies inbound Resend webhook signatures             |
| `RESEND_FROM_EMAIL`         | Server  | Sender address; must be on a domain verified in Resend |
| `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` | Server  | Edge Functions and the demo seed script only           |

`PUBLIC_*` names are read via SvelteKit's `$env/static/public` at build time; there is no `VITE_`
prefixing. Server-only values are read via `$env/static/private` (or `process.env` in scripts) and
never reach the browser.

This repo's `.env` is generated by the 1Password CLI, which is why `npm run dev` is

1	# YFL Expense Tracker
2	
3	Family expense tracking app built with SvelteKit 2, Svelte 5, Supabase, and Tailwind CSS 4.
4	
5	## Commands
6	
7	```bash
8	npm run dev          # Dev server on localhost:5173
9	npm run build        # Production build
10	npm run check        # Type checking (svelte-check)
11	npm run test:unit    # Vitest unit tests
12	npm run test:e2e     # Playwright e2e tests
13	npm test             # Full test suite (unit + e2e)
14	npm run lint         # Prettier check + ESLint
15	npm run format       # Auto-format with Prettier
16	```
17	
18	## Architecture
19	
20	- **Routes:** `src/routes/` — SvelteKit file-based routing
21	- **Services:** `src/lib/services/` — Business logic (ExpenseService, ReceiptService, etc.). Some use DI (take Supabase client as param), others use singleton pattern with module-level import.
22	- **Models:** `src/lib/models/` — TypeScript data models
23	- **Components:** `src/lib/components/` — Reusable Svelte components
24	- **Utils:** `src/lib/utils/` — Helper functions with co-located `.spec.ts` tests
25	- **Server:** `src/lib/server/` — Server-only code (file validation, OCR processing)
26	- **CSV Parsers:** `src/lib/services/csvParsers/` — Bank-specific CSV parsers (Amex, PC Financial, RBC, TD, Simplii, EQ Bank, Wealth Simple) with `BaseCSVParser` and `CSVParserFactory` for auto-detection
27	- **Docs:** `docs/` — Project documentation. `docs/adr/` (architecture decision records), `docs/plans/` (design docs), `docs/prd-*.md` (active PRDs — in-file `**Status:**` front-matter carries the detail; **when a PRD is finished, `git mv` it to `docs/prd-done/`** so done-vs-active is visible from `ls` without opening files, and fix its now-one-level-deeper relative links plus any inbound links), `docs/product-backlog.md` (the single working list — features, bugs, engineering, and open refactoring items as one-liners) plus `docs/refactoring-backlog.md` (detailed RF-NN reference, not a separate to-do list), `docs/domain-model.md` (ubiquitous-language glossary). Prefer `docs/` over root for any new note or plan; the root keeps only `README.md` and `CLAUDE.md`.
28	- **Migrations:** `supabase/migrations/` — SQL migrations (schema + RLS policies)
29	
30	## Supabase Migrations
31	
32	Migrations live in `supabase/migrations/` as numbered SQL files. The project is linked to the remote Supabase project (`YFL Expense Tracker`, region `ca-central-1`).
33	
34	```bash
35	supabase migration list           # Show local vs remote migration status
36	supabase db push                  # Push pending migrations to remote database
37	supabase db push --dry-run        # Preview what would be applied without running
38	supabase migration new <name>     # Create a new empty migration file
39	supabase db diff --schema public  # Generate migration from local schema changes
40	supabase db reset                 # Reset local DB and re-run all migrations (destructive)
41	```
42	
43	**Naming convention:** `YYYYMMDD_description.sql` (e.g. `20260225_secure_receipts_storage.sql`).
44	
45	**Squashed to a baseline (2026-07-26).** `supabase/migrations/` holds one file,
46	`20260726120000_baseline.sql`; the 31 predecessors are in `supabase/migrations-archive/`. They
47	could not rebuild the DB from scratch — replay died at `007` with `relation "public.families" does
48	not exist` because `families` was created by hand in the dashboard and only captured later by the
49	`20251010000319_remote_schema.sql` dump, which sorts _after_ `007`. Prod history was repaired to
50	match (bookkeeping only). **The baseline's storage section is hand-maintained** — `supabase db
51	dump` does not cover the `storage` schema, so the `receipts` bucket + its 4 policies are appended
52	manually at the end of the file. Any storage change must be reflected there too. Verify every new
53	migration with `npm run db:reset` before pushing. See `docs/local-dev.md`.
54	
55	**Important:** The migration role does NOT own `storage.objects`, so `COMMENT ON POLICY` and `ALTER TABLE` on storage tables will fail. Stick to `CREATE POLICY` / `DROP POLICY` / `UPDATE storage.buckets` for storage changes.
56	
57	## Key Patterns
58	
59	- **Expenses are computed, not stored.** No "expenses" table — expenses are joins of receipts + expense_categories + categories. Each receipt maps to exactly one expense (1:1).
60	- **All data is family-scoped.** Users belong to families via `family_members`. RLS policies enforce family-level access on receipts, transactions, categories, and vendor rules.
61	- **Receipt storage is private.** The `receipts` bucket is private — all file access uses signed URLs via `getSignedReceiptUrl()` from `src/lib/utils/signedUrl.ts`. Pages cache signed URLs in a reactive `signedUrls` map loaded via `$effect`. OCR uses short-lived signed URLs (5 min expiry). Display uses 1-hour expiry.
62	- **Storage RLS is family-scoped for reads.** Family members can read each other's receipt files. Write/delete is restricted to the file owner (path prefix = `user_id`).
63	- **Auto-categorization:** Vendor rules map normalized merchant names to categories. Applied on page load for uncategorized expenses. Normalization: lowercase, strip special chars, trim.
64	- **Date pickers use flowbite-svelte.** Always use `<Datepicker>` from `flowbite-svelte` with `toDate()` and `toISODateString()` helpers from `$lib/utils/dateConversion`. Never use raw `<input type="date">`.
65	- **Never use `new Date("YYYY-MM-DD")` for date-only strings.** JavaScript parses bare date strings as UTC midnight, which shifts to the previous day in timezones west of UTC. Always use `toDate()` to parse or `formatDate()` to display — both from `$lib/utils/dateConversion`. These parse year/month/day parts manually to construct local-time Date objects.
66	- **Date filters preserved in URL** via `preserveFilters()` helper in `+layout.svelte`.
67	- **Version tracking** in `src/lib/version.ts`. Increment by 0.01 for small changes, 0.1 for features — but **only bump the version when the change is actually committed and pushed live.** Leave `version.ts` (and any version tag in the docs) untouched for uncommitted, in-progress work; the human assigns the number at commit time. Don't write a specific version tag (e.g. "v0.70") in design docs / the backlog for unreleased work — use "(pending release)" instead.
68	- **Transaction amounts: negative = expense, positive = refund/credit.** This matches the UI display (red = negative = expense, green = positive = credit). Most banks (PC Financial, EQ Bank, RBC, TD, Simplii) already use negative for expenses so parsers keep signs as-is (`invertSign: false`). Only American Express uses positive for expenses and needs `invertSign: true`. Wealth Simple CSV exports have inconsistent signs across downloads, so the parser uses the `type` column (Purchase → negative, Payment/Refund → positive) instead of `invertSign`. See `BaseCSVParser.normalizeAmount()`.
69	- **XLS/XLSX import supported.** Excel files are converted to CSV via `ExcelToCSVConverter` (SheetJS) before passing through the same parser pipeline. File type detected by extension/MIME.
70	
71	## Gotchas
72	
73	- Dual test environments: browser tests use Playwright provider, server tests use Node.js — configured in `vite.config.ts` under `test.projects`
74	- PDFs go directly to Mistral Vision API (pixtral-12b) — no conversion needed
75	- Suspicious date flag triggers for receipts >42 days old or future-dated
76	- Multi-email support: primary email in `auth.users`, up to 5 additional in `profiles` table. Email receipt ingestion checks both.
77	- File uploads: JPEG/PNG/HEIC up to 5MB, PDF up to 10MB. Validated client-side and server-side (`src/lib/server/fileValidation.ts`)
78	- Recent migrations (Jan–Feb 2026) refactored family-scoping, fixed RLS recursion issues, and secured storage — be careful modifying RLS policies
79	- Receipt image URLs are async (signed URLs). Components use `$effect` + `Promise.then()` to load them, not synchronous calls. Never use `getPublicUrl()`.
80	- Transaction imports accept CSV, XLS, and XLSX files. Excel files are read as ArrayBuffer and converted to CSV text before parsing.

1	# Local development
2	
3	A full Supabase stack (Postgres + Auth + PostgREST + Storage) runs on your machine, so day-to-day
4	development never touches production data. Set up once, then it is two commands.
5	
6	## One-time setup
7	
8	1. **Install OrbStack** — `brew install --cask orbstack`, then **launch it once**. First launch is
9	   what installs the CLI tools into `~/.orbstack/bin`, starts the VM, and takes over
10	   `/var/run/docker.sock`. Until you open it, nothing works and `docker` is not on your PATH.
11	
12	   OrbStack is used instead of Docker Desktop: the Supabase CLI needs a Docker socket, and OrbStack
13	   provides a standard one with no configuration, starts on demand in seconds, and has none of
14	   Docker Desktop's update churn. If Docker Desktop was installed before, uninstall it first so the
15	   two do not fight over the socket. OrbStack repoints the socket and switches the Docker context
16	   itself.
17	
18	2. `npm install`
19	
20	## Daily use
21	
22	```bash
23	npm run db:up        # start the local Supabase stack
24	npm run dev:local    # app on localhost:5173, pointed at the local stack
25	```
26	
27	| Command                    | What it does                                                         |
28	| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
29	| `npm run db:up`            | Start the local stack                                                |
30	| `npm run db:down`          | Stop it                                                              |
31	| `npm run db:reset`         | Drop and rebuild the database from the baseline migration            |
32	| `npm run db:studio`        | Open Supabase Studio (<http://127.0.0.1:54323>)                      |
33	| `npm run dev:local`        | Dev server against the local stack                                   |
34	| `npm run dev`              | Dev server against **production** — deliberate, rarely what you want |
35	| `npm run seed:demo:local`  | Seed the demo family locally                                         |
36	| `npm run test:integration` | Run the RLS integration tests against the local stack                |
37	
38	`dev:local` and friends go through the `local:env` script, which injects the local API URL, anon
39	key, and service-role key. Those are Supabase's fixed local development defaults — the same on
40	every machine, not secrets — which is why they are checked in and why local work needs no
41	1Password. Only `npm run dev` (production) uses `op run --env-file=.env`.
42	
43	Note that `dev:local` does not set `MISTRAL_API_KEY`, so OCR will fail locally with a clear error.
44	That is deliberate: OCR calls a paid third-party API and most work does not need it. To exercise
45	OCR, prefix the command with the key from 1Password.
46	
47	Local ports: API `54321`, Postgres `54322`, Studio `54323`, mail catcher `54324`.
48	
49	## Getting data to look at
50	
51	```bash
52	npm run seed:demo:local
53	```
54	
55	Builds the self-contained "Sample Family (DEMO)" — two users, ~150 receipts across 2025 and
56	Jan–Jul 2026, ~97 transactions, and one instance of every notable edge state. It prints a randomly
57	generated password to log in with. See [Demo data seed](demo-seed.md).
58	
59	A clean slate is `npm run db:reset && npm run seed:demo:local`.
60	
61	## The schema baseline
62	
63	`supabase/migrations/` holds **one** file: `20260726120000_baseline.sql`.
64	
65	The 31 migrations that preceded it are in `supabase/migrations-archive/` (and in git history). They
66	were squashed on 2026-07-26 because **they could not rebuild the database from scratch**: replay
67	died at `007_transactions_table.sql` with `relation "public.families" does not exist`, since
68	`families` was created out-of-band in the dashboard and only captured later by the retroactive
69	`20251010000319_remote_schema.sql` dump — which sorts _after_ `007`. That made local stacks and new
70	cloud environments impossible to create, and left the migration chain permanently unverifiable.
71	
72	The baseline is a `supabase db dump` of production's `public` schema, plus a hand-maintained
73	storage section at the end. **The storage section matters:** `supabase db dump` does not cover the
74	`storage` schema, so the `receipts` bucket and its four policies are written out by hand. Anything
75	that changes storage must be added there as well as in a new migration.
76	
77	Production's migration history was repaired to match (the 31 old versions marked `reverted`, the
78	baseline marked `applied`). No schema or data changed — only the bookkeeping in
79	`supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`. `supabase db push --dry-run` reports the remote as up to
80	date.
81	
82	From here, normal migration practice resumes: `supabase migration new <name>`, edit, `db:reset` to
83	verify it replays clean, then `supabase db push`.
84	
85	## Testing
86	
87	- `npm run test:unit` — no backend needed.
88	- `npm run test:e2e` — seam-only; builds against fake public config and never authenticates, so it
89	  needs neither secrets nor a running stack. Leave it that way.
90	- `npm run test:integration` — needs `npm run db:up`. Runs the RLS suites that verify family
91	  scoping, cross-member visibility, and unique constraints against a real Postgres. Before the
92	  baseline these could never run at all.
93	
94	## What still is not local
95	
96	- **Edge Functions.** `supabase functions serve` needs the local stack (now available) but the
97	  Resend webhook also needs a public URL for inbound webhooks. Keep debugging deliveries via
98	  <https://resend.com/webhooks>.
99	- **Real email delivery.** Auth emails land in the local mail catcher on `:54324`; nothing leaves
100	  your machine.
101	
102	## Troubleshooting
103	
104	- **`Cannot connect to the Docker daemon`** — OrbStack is not running, or has never been launched.
105	  Open it. Check with `docker context ls`; the current context should be `orbstack`.
106	- **Strange errors after a Supabase CLI upgrade** — the CLI is pinned to an exact version in
107	  `package.json` for this reason. If you do upgrade: `supabase stop --no-backup`, upgrade, then
108	  `supabase start`. Never upgrade with containers running.
109	- **`supabase start` is slow the first time** — it pulls several GB of images. Subsequent starts
110	  take seconds.

- **`.env` is a FIFO, so nothing can read it twice.** `npm run dev` works only because `op run --env-file=.env` consumes the named pipe and injects the values; a bare `vite build`, a second reader, or any tool expecting a regular file gets nothing. This is why `playwright.config.ts` hard-codes fake public config and why the local scripts inline Supabase's well-known local defaults instead of using an env file. Worth knowing before adding any new tooling that expects to read `.env`.

## What happened

**OrbStack was the easy half.** It had never been launched, which is why `docker` wasn't on PATH. **Then `supabase start` found the real problem.** Replay onto an empty database died at `007_transactions_table.sql`: `relation "public.families" does not exist`. `families` was created by hand in the dashboard and only captured months later by the retroactive `20251010000319_remote_schema.sql` dump — which sorts *after* `007`. The database could not be rebuilt from its own migrations. Not locally, not in a new cloud project. Production was a one-off artifact.

**Squashed to a baseline**, per your call. `20260726120000_baseline.sql` = a `db dump` of prod's `public` schema plus a hand-written storage section (`db dump` doesn't cover the `storage` schema, so the `receipts` bucket and its four policies are appended manually — that's a maintenance obligation, now flagged in `CLAUDE.md`). The 31 old files are in `supabase/migrations-archive/` via `git mv`, so history is intact.

**Production history repaired.** 31 versions → `reverted`, baseline → `applied`. Bookkeeping only; backup at `.scratch/prod-migration-history-backup-20260726.sql` (78KB, all rows with their SQL). `db push --dry-run` now reports the remote up to date — schema and data untouched.

So no environment could be built from `supabase/migrations/` — not a local stack, not a fresh cloud project — `supabase db reset` was unusable, the migrations were permanently unverifiable, and prod was a one-off artifact with no reproducible provenance. **Fixed by squashing to a single baseline:** `20260726120000_baseline.sql` (a `supabase db dump` of prod's `public` schema plus a hand-written storage section, since `db dump` does not cover the `storage` schema); the 31 predecessors moved to `supabase/migrations-archive/`; `supabase db reset` verified green twice (11 tables, 29 public policies, 10 functions, 4 storage policies, private `receipts` bucket); demo seed and the RLS integration suite both pass against it. Suite now 1431 passed / 8 skipped.

55:- **⚠️ The profile page's family-members RPC is untested; the harness mock lacks `.rpc()`.** Running `profile-page.svelte.spec.ts` prints `Error loading family members: [TypeError: supabase.rpc is not a function]`. The page was right and the test was stale: dropped the `user-42` assertion and replaced it with a `Primary Email` label check, so the section still has real coverage rather than just losing an assertion. Suite now 1431 passed / 8 skipped.
54:- **Prettier green again. ✅ DONE.** The five committed docs that failed `prettier --check` as of `HEAD` (`email-notifications.md`, `prd-mobile-capture.md`, `prd-family-invitations.md`, `prd-done/prd-security-remediation.md`, `prd-done/prd-type-check-cleanup.md`) were reformatted. No prose was altered. `npm run lint` passes. **This is the second time the green state has rotted** — it will keep rotting until the CI gate below exists.

# Local development

A full Supabase stack (Postgres + Auth + PostgREST + Storage) runs on your machine, so day-to-day
development never touches production data. Set up once, then it is two commands.

## One-time setup

1. **Install OrbStack** — `brew install --cask orbstack`, then **launch it once**. First launch is
   what installs the CLI tools into `~/.orbstack/bin`, starts the VM, and takes over
   `/var/run/docker.sock`. Until you open it, nothing works and `docker` is not on your PATH.

   OrbStack is used instead of Docker Desktop: the Supabase CLI needs a Docker socket, and OrbStack
   provides a standard one with no configuration, starts on demand in seconds, and has none of
   Docker Desktop's update churn. If Docker Desktop was installed before, uninstall it first so the
   two do not fight over the socket. OrbStack repoints the socket and switches the Docker context
   itself.

2. `npm install`

## Daily use

```bash
npm run db:up        # start the local Supabase stack
npm run dev:local    # app on localhost:5173, pointed at the local stack
```

| Command                    | What it does                                                         |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `npm run db:up`            | Start the local stack                                                |
| `npm run db:down`          | Stop it                                                              |
| `npm run db:reset`         | Drop and rebuild the database from the baseline migration            |
| `npm run db:studio`        | Open Supabase Studio (<http://127.0.0.1:54323>)                      |
| `npm run dev:local`        | Dev server against the local stack                                   |
| `npm run dev`              | Dev server against **production** — deliberate, rarely what you want |
| `npm run seed:demo:local`  | Seed the demo family locally                                         |
| `npm run test:integration` | Run the RLS integration tests against the local stack                |

`dev:local` and friends go through the `local:env` script, which injects the local API URL, anon
key, and service-role key. Those are Supabase's fixed local development defaults — the same on
every machine, not secrets — which is why they are checked in and why local work needs no
1Password. Only `npm run dev` (production) uses `op run --env-file=.env`.

Note that `dev:local` does not set `MISTRAL_API_KEY`, so OCR will fail locally with a clear error.
That is deliberate: OCR calls a paid third-party API and most work does not need it. To exercise
OCR, prefix the command with the key from 1Password.

Local ports: API `54321`, Postgres `54322`, Studio `54323`, mail catcher `54324`.

## Getting data to look at

```bash
npm run seed:demo:local
```

Builds the self-contained "Sample Family (DEMO)" — two users, ~150 receipts across 2025 and
Jan–Jul 2026, ~97 transactions, and one instance of every notable edge state. It prints a randomly
generated password to log in with. See [Demo data seed](demo-seed.md).

A clean slate is `npm run db:reset && npm run seed:demo:local`.

## The schema baseline

`supabase/migrations/` holds **one** file: `20260726120000_baseline.sql`.

The 31 migrations that preceded it are in `supabase/migrations-archive/` (and in git history). They
were squashed on 2026-07-26 because **they could not rebuild the database from scratch**: replay
died at `007_transactions_table.sql` with `relation "public.families" does not exist`, since
`families` was created out-of-band in the dashboard and only captured later by the retroactive
`20251010000319_remote_schema.sql` dump — which sorts _after_ `007`. That made local stacks and new
cloud environments impossible to create, and left the migration chain permanently unverifiable.

The baseline is a `supabase db dump` of production's `public` schema, plus a hand-maintained
storage section at the end. **The storage section matters:** `supabase db dump` does not cover the
`storage` schema, so the `receipts` bucket and its four policies are written out by hand. Anything
that changes storage must be added there as well as in a new migration.

Production's migration history was repaired to match (the 31 old versions marked `reverted`, the
baseline marked `applied`). No schema or data changed — only the bookkeeping in
`supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`. `supabase db push --dry-run` reports the remote as up to
date.

From here, normal migration practice resumes: `supabase migration new <name>`, edit, `db:reset` to
verify it replays clean, then `supabase db push`.

## Testing

- `npm run test:unit` — no backend needed.
- `npm run test:e2e` — seam-only; builds against fake public config and never authenticates, so it
  needs neither secrets nor a running stack. Leave it that way.
- `npm run test:integration` — needs `npm run db:up`. Runs the RLS suites that verify family
  scoping, cross-member visibility, and unique constraints against a real Postgres. Before the
  baseline these could never run at all.

## What still is not local

- **Edge Functions.** `supabase functions serve` needs the local stack (now available) but the
  Resend webhook also needs a public URL for inbound webhooks. Keep debugging deliveries via
  <https://resend.com/webhooks>.
- **Real email delivery.** Auth emails land in the local mail catcher on `:54324`; nothing leaves
  your machine.

## Troubleshooting

- **`Cannot connect to the Docker daemon`** — OrbStack is not running, or has never been launched.
  Open it. Check with `docker context ls`; the current context should be `orbstack`.
- **Strange errors after a Supabase CLI upgrade** — the CLI is pinned to an exact version in
  `package.json` for this reason. If you do upgrade: `supabase stop --no-backup`, upgrade, then
  `supabase start`. Never upgrade with containers running.
- **`supabase start` is slow the first time** — it pulls several GB of images. Subsequent starts
  take seconds.

# YFL Family Expense Tracker

A browser-first expense tracking and reconciliation app for a family: scan receipts,
import bank/credit-card statements, match the two, and report on spending.

Built with SvelteKit 2, Svelte 5 (runes), Supabase (Postgres + Auth + Storage), Tailwind CSS 4,
and Mistral Vision for OCR.

## What it does

- **Receipts** — upload JPEG/PNG/HEIC (≤5MB) or PDF (≤10MB), singly or in bulk. Images are
  resized client-side before upload. OCR runs server-side and auto-fills merchant, date, total,
  tax, card, and currency. Manual entry and inline editing are also supported, as are receipt
  splits (one receipt across several categories).
- **Email ingestion** — forward a receipt to a Resend-hosted address and a Supabase Edge Function
  ingests it automatically.
- **Transactions** — import bank and credit-card statements as CSV, XLS, or XLSX. Bank-specific
  parsers auto-detect the format: Amex, EQ Bank, PC Financial, RBC, Simplii, TD, Wealth Simple.
- **Reconciliation** — match receipts to transactions, flag duplicates, exclude transactions.
- **Categorization** — family-shared categories with vendor rules that auto-categorize by
  normalized merchant name.
- **Spending** — a category/Area-of-Importance hierarchy with year-to-date and
  compare-to-prior-year views.
- **Export** — CSV and PDF from the Expenses page.
- **Multi-currency** — foreign-currency receipts carry an exchange rate.

Everything is **family-scoped**: users belong to a family via `family_members`, and Postgres RLS
policies enforce that all receipts, transactions, categories, and vendor rules are visible to the
whole family and to nobody else.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 22+ (developed on 26)
- A Supabase project (free tier is fine)
- A Mistral API key (for OCR)
- Optional: a Resend account (for email receipt ingestion and notification emails)
- Optional: the [1Password CLI](https://developer.1password.com/docs/cli/) (`op`) — see
  [Environment variables](#environment-variables)

## Local development

A full Supabase stack runs on your machine, so development never touches production data. Install
[OrbStack](https://orbstack.dev) and **launch it once**, then:

```bash
npm install
npm run db:up            # start the local Supabase stack
npm run seed:demo:local  # populate it with the demo family
npm run dev:local        # app on localhost:5173, against the local stack
```

`npm run dev` (no `:local`) points at **production**. Full details, commands, and troubleshooting:
**[docs/local-dev.md](docs/local-dev.md)**.

## Deploying to a new Supabase project

### 1. Create the project

1. Create a project at <https://supabase.com>.
2. From Project Settings → API, note the **Project URL**, the **anon public key**, and the
   **service role key** (the service role key is for Edge Functions and the seed script only —
   never ship it to the browser).
3. Under Authentication → Providers, enable **Email** (email/password).

### 2. Apply the schema

```bash
supabase login
supabase link --project-ref <your-project-ref>
supabase db push --dry-run   # preview
supabase db push
```

`supabase/migrations/` holds a single baseline migration that builds the whole schema, including
the private `receipts` bucket and its policies — there is nothing to create by hand. The 31
migrations it replaced are archived in `supabase/migrations-archive/`; see
[docs/local-dev.md](docs/local-dev.md#the-schema-baseline) for why they were squashed.

The bucket must stay **private**: all file access goes through signed URLs
(`getSignedReceiptUrl()` in `src/lib/utils/signedUrl.ts`); the app never calls `getPublicUrl()`.

## Environment variables

| Variable                    | Scope   | Purpose                                                |
| --------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`       | Browser | Supabase project URL                                   |
| `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`  | Browser | Supabase anon key                                      |
| `MISTRAL_API_KEY`           | Server  | OCR via Mistral Vision                                 |
| `RESEND_API_KEY`            | Server  | Email receipt ingestion + notification emails          |
| `RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET`     | Server  | Verifies inbound Resend webhook signatures             |
| `RESEND_FROM_EMAIL`         | Server  | Sender address; must be on a domain verified in Resend |
| `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` | Server  | Edge Functions and the demo seed script only           |

`PUBLIC_*` names are read via SvelteKit's `$env/static/public` at build time; there is no `VITE_`
prefixing. Server-only values are read via `$env/static/private` (or `process.env` in scripts) and
never reach the browser.

This repo's `.env` is generated by the 1Password CLI, which is why `npm run dev` is
`op run --env-file=.env -- vite dev`. If you are not using 1Password, write a plain `.env` with the
variables above and run `vite dev` directly — `.env` and `.env.*` are gitignored.

## Install and run

```bash
npm install
npm run dev      # http://localhost:5173
```

Create your first user in Supabase → Authentication → Add user, then sign in at `/login`. Passwords
must be 16+ characters with at least one upper, lower, digit, and special character.

For a populated app to click around in, see [`docs/demo-seed.md`](docs/demo-seed.md):
`npm run seed:demo` builds a self-contained "Sample Family (DEMO)" with ~150 receipts, ~95
transactions, and one instance of every notable edge state.

## Commands

```bash
npm run dev              # Dev server against PRODUCTION
npm run dev:local        # Dev server against the local Supabase stack
npm run db:up            # Start the local stack   (db:down, db:reset, db:studio)
npm run build            # Production build
npm run check            # Type checking (svelte-check)
npm run test:unit        # Vitest unit tests (browser + node projects)
npm run test:e2e         # Playwright e2e tests
npm run test:integration # RLS integration tests (needs db:up)
npm test                 # Full suite (unit + e2e)
npm run lint             # Prettier check + ESLint
npm run format           # Auto-format with Prettier
npm run seed:demo:local  # Seed the demo family locally (see docs/demo-seed.md)
```

Unit tests need no backend. The e2e suite is seam-only — it builds against fake public config and
never authenticates or hits a real Supabase, so it runs with no secrets.

The RLS integration tests (e.g. `src/lib/tests/family-category-visibility.spec.ts`) need a real
Postgres — they **skip themselves** unless `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` and `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`
are set, so they never run in the default suite. `npm run test:integration` points them at the
local stack; never point them at production.

## Email receipts (Resend → Supabase Edge Function)

`supabase/functions/resend/index.ts` receives Resend webhooks, looks up the sender against
`auth.users` plus the additional addresses in `profiles`, extracts the receipt (email body first,
then attachments) with Mistral, and writes the receipt and its file into Supabase.

```bash
supabase functions deploy resend --no-verify-jwt
supabase secrets set MISTRAL_API_KEY=… RESEND_API_KEY=… RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET=… RESEND_FROM_EMAIL=…
```

Then in the Resend dashboard add a webhook pointing at
`https://<project-ref>.functions.supabase.co/resend` for the `email.received` event, and copy its
signing secret into `RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. The endpoint fails closed: `401` on signature
mismatch, `500` if the secret is not configured.

See [`docs/email-notifications.md`](docs/email-notifications.md) for the notification side and for
debugging via the Resend dashboard.

## Multiple email addresses

Each user has one primary email in `auth.users` and up to five more in `profiles`, so receipts can
be forwarded from work, personal, or a partner's address. Ingestion checks both. See
[`docs/profile-emails.md`](docs/profile-emails.md).

## Architecture and documentation

The authoritative architecture notes, key patterns, and gotchas live in
[`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) — read it before changing anything non-trivial. In particular: expenses
are computed (there is no `expenses` table), all date handling goes through
`$lib/utils/dateConversion`, and negative transaction amounts mean expense.

- [`docs/domain-model.md`](docs/domain-model.md) — ubiquitous-language glossary
- [`docs/product-backlog.md`](docs/product-backlog.md) — the single working list
- [`docs/adr/`](docs/adr/) — architecture decision records
- [`docs/plans/`](docs/plans/) — design docs
- [`docs/prd-*.md`](docs/) — active PRDs; finished ones move to [`docs/prd-done/`](docs/prd-done/)
- [`docs/refactoring-backlog.md`](docs/refactoring-backlog.md) — detailed RF-NN reference

Database schema is defined by the migrations in `supabase/migrations/`; that is the reference, not
a table in this file.

## Troubleshooting

- **403 or CORS on receipt images** — the `receipts` bucket must exist and be private, and the
  storage policies from the migrations must be applied. Images load asynchronously via signed URLs;
  a synchronous `getPublicUrl()` will not work.
- **RLS errors on insert** — confirm you are authenticated and belong to a family
  (`family_members`). Family scoping, not user scoping, is what the policies check.
- **OCR failures** — verify `MISTRAL_API_KEY` and your Mistral quota. OCR runs server-side at
  `/api/ocr`; check the server console, not the browser.
- **Email receipts not arriving** — start at <https://resend.com/webhooks>: it shows the signing
  secret and the status our function returned. Then check
  `SELECT find_user_by_email('sender@example.com');` and
  `supabase functions logs resend --tail`.
- **Notification emails return 403 "Request is forbidden"** — `RESEND_FROM_EMAIL` is not on a
  domain verified in Resend.
- **A receipt is flagged with a suspicious date** — receipts more than 42 days old or dated in the
  future are flagged deliberately.
